intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Raiders line gives up a sack on 10.4% of dropbacks (31st), and the Chargers get home on 8.1% (5th).
The Raiders score 14.2 points a game (32nd in the league), and the Chargers allow 19.8 (8th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chargers.

other_side.title: When the Chargers have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chargers gain 4.8 yards (21st), while the Raiders give up 4.8 (11th).
The Chargers line gives up a sack on 9.1% of dropbacks (29th), and the Raiders get home on 6.0% (21st).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Raiders, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Raiders are 11th in yards per play allowed (4.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Raiders score 14 or more in the first half, the Chargers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 74% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chargers win about 74 of them. That means the Raiders win 26, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Chargers by 8.5, about 77%. I'm at 74%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Raiders win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Steelers offense ranks 17th, the Patriots defense ranks 3rd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Gillette Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, NE have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Steelers score 22.4 points a game (17th in the league), and the Patriots allow 17.9 (3rd).
On a typical play the Steelers gain 4.9 yards (19th), while the Patriots give up 4.6 (6th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: On a typical play the Patriots gain 5.7 yards (3rd), while the Steelers give up 5.3 (21st).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 8.8% of dropbacks (27th), and the Steelers get home on 6.9% (10th).
So the Patriots have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Steelers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Steelers score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Steelers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 68% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Patriots win about 68 of them. That means the Steelers win 32, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Patriots by 4.5, about 66%. I'm at 68%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Steelers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.

On top of that, DET have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Lions score 28.3 points a game (4th in the league), and the Jets allow 29.6 (31st).

That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Jets have the ball

So the Lions have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Packers at 55%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Buccaneers offense ranks 29th, the Packers defense ranks 14th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? Over the last three games, GB and TB have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Buccaneers gain 4.3 yards (29th), while the Packers give up 4.9 (14th).
The Buccaneers line gives up a sack on 10.6% of dropbacks (32nd), and the Packers get home on 6.0% (20th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Packers.

other_side.title: When the Packers have the ball
body: On a typical play the Packers gain 4.6 yards (20th), while the Buccaneers give up 4.6 (10th).

items.lead: TB have been playing better lately.
items.text: Over the last three games, TB have won more often than GB, and their scoring margin is about 10 points a game better.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Buccaneers are 10th in yards per play allowed (4.6). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Buccaneers score 14 or more in the first half, the Packers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Vikings at 74%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Dolphins offense ranks 31st, the Vikings defense ranks 2nd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? The game is at U.S. Bank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, MIN have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Dolphins score 12.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Vikings allow 13.7 (2nd).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (30th), and the Vikings get home on 10.5% (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings score 23.7 points a game (16th in the league), and the Dolphins allow 28.7 (28th).
So the Vikings have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: MIN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for MIA in this game.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, rest and weather are about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Rams line gives up a sack on 3.0% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Bills get home on 6.0% (17th).
On a typical play the Rams gain 5.9 yards (5th), while the Bills give up 5.1 (15th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Rams.

other_side.title: When the Bills have the ball
body: The Bills score 31.8 points a game (1st in the league), and the Rams allow 20.8 (9th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bills, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bills would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Rams have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bills win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bears at 61%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bears offense ranks 10th, the Falcons defense ranks 24th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? Over the last three games, CHI and ATL have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.
On top of that, CHI have the better scoring margin.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bears line gives up a sack on 5.3% of dropbacks (10th), and the Falcons get home on 5.2% (24th).
The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Falcons allow 24.4 (21st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bears.

other_side.title: When the Falcons have the ball
body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.7 yards (6th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
The Falcons line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
So the Bears have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Falcons are 6th in yards per play (5.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Falcons would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Falcons win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.

On top of that, IND are at home.

body: The Titans score 11.6 points a game (32nd in the league), and the Colts allow 27.6 (28th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Colts.

other_side.title: When the Colts have the ball
body: On a typical play the Colts gain 4.4 yards (23rd), while the Titans give up 4.9 (13th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Titans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The offenses have been about even.
items.text: Over the last three games, TEN and IND have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 11th in points allowed per game (21.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Colts defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Broncos at 69%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Cardinals offense ranks 31st, the Broncos defense ranks 17th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? DEN are 2-1 over their last three games; ARI are 0-3. They also have about 14 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.2 yards (31st), while the Broncos give up 5.0 (17th).
The Cardinals score 21.6 points a game (22nd in the league), and the Broncos allow 22.2 (14th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Broncos.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 3.7% of dropbacks (4th), and the Cardinals get home on 6.6% (14th).
So the Broncos have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: DEN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for ARI in this game.

items.lead: ARI's offense has been more productive.
items.text: Over the last three games, ARI have gained slightly more on a typical play than DEN, scoring 25 points a game to DEN's 22. Expect ARI to move the ball more consistently.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Cardinals score 14 or more in the first half, the Broncos defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Patriots at 57%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Dolphins offense ranks 31st, the Patriots defense ranks 4th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? NE are 2-1 over their last three games; MIA are 0-3. They also have about 9 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, rest tilts toward NE.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Dolphins score 14.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Patriots allow 18.8 (4th).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Patriots get home on 5.9% (19th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: On a typical play the Patriots gain 5.5 yards (9th), while the Dolphins give up 5.5 (26th).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (17th), and the Dolphins get home on 1.9% (32nd).
So the Patriots have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 57% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Patriots win about 57 of them. That means the Dolphins win 43, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 55%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Lions offense ranks 1st, the Dolphins defense ranks 24th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? DET are 2-1 over their last three games; MIA are 0-3. They also have about 17 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Lions score 32.8 points a game (1st in the league), and the Dolphins allow 26.4 (24th).
On a typical play the Lions gain 5.6 yards (8th), while the Dolphins give up 5.5 (26th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Dolphins have the ball
body: The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Lions get home on 8.0% (6th).
So the Lions have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Lions win about 55 of them. That means the Dolphins win 45, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at FC Bayern Munich Stadium, a neutral site, but my model still gives DET the standard home-team bump of about 5.9 points of win chance.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.6 yards (8th), while the Patriots give up 4.8 (12th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: On a typical play the Patriots gain 5.5 yards (9th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (25th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Patriots, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Patriots are 4th in points allowed per game (18.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Patriots would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Patriots win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the 49ers at 59%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Vikings offense ranks 24th, the 49ers defense ranks 5th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Estadio Banorte, a neutral site, but my model still gives SF the standard home-team bump of about 5.9 points of win chance.
On top of that, SF have the better scoring margin.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Vikings gain 4.4 yards (24th), while the 49ers give up 4.3 (5th).
The Vikings score 21.8 points a game (20th in the league), and the 49ers allow 18.6 (3rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the 49ers have the ball
body: The 49ers line gives up a sack on 1.7% of dropbacks (1st), and the Vikings get home on 9.1% (4th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Vikings are 1st in points allowed per game (12.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Vikings would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Vikings score 14 or more in the first half, the 49ers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Vikings win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the 49ers win about 59 of them. That means the Vikings win 41, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Vikings win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 53%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Lions offense ranks 8th, the Bears defense ranks 27th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Ford Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.6 yards (8th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
The Lions line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (15th), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Bears have the ball
body: The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Lions allow 29.6 (29th).
On a typical play the Bears gain 5.0 yards (16th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (25th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bears, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bears are 5th in points allowed per game (19.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bears would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bears win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Lions win about 53 of them. That means the Bears win 47, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bears win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at State Farm Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Eagles line gives up a sack on 7.5% of dropbacks (25th), and the Cardinals get home on 6.6% (14th).

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Eagles, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: PHI have the better scoring margin.
items.text: Both teams are 0-3 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: PHI have about 5 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Eagles would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Eagles score 14 or more in the first half, the Cardinals defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Eagles win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Patriots at 56%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Vikings offense ranks 20th, the Patriots defense ranks 4th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Gillette Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Vikings score 21.8 points a game (20th in the league), and the Patriots allow 18.8 (4th).
On a typical play the Vikings gain 4.4 yards (24th), while the Patriots give up 4.8 (12th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Patriots.

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball
body: The Patriots score 22.0 points a game (18th in the league), and the Vikings allow 12.8 (1st).
The Patriots line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (17th), and the Vikings get home on 9.1% (4th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Vikings, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Vikings are 1st in points allowed per game (12.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Vikings would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Vikings score 14 or more in the first half, the Patriots defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Vikings win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 56% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Patriots win about 56 of them. That means the Vikings win 44, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Vikings win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Panthers at 53%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Panthers offense ranks 7th, the Bengals defense ranks 22nd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Bank of America Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, rest and weather are about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Panthers gain 5.6 yards (7th), while the Bengals give up 5.2 (22nd).
The Panthers line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (14th), and the Bengals get home on 9.3% (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Panthers.

other_side.title: When the Bengals have the ball
body: The Bengals line gives up a sack on 4.5% of dropbacks (7th), and the Panthers get home on 5.0% (25th).
The Bengals score 25.6 points a game (10th in the league), and the Panthers allow 27.2 (27th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Bengals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: CIN's offense is heating up.
items.text: Over the last three games, CIN have gained noticeably more on a typical play than CAR. That offense has been one of the best in the league right now. Expect CIN to move the ball more consistently.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Bengals are 10th in points per game (25.6). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Panthers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Bengals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Panthers win about 53 of them. That means the Bengals win 47, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bengals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 57%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Lions offense ranks 8th, the Giants defense ranks 23rd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Ford Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, DET have the better scoring margin.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.6 yards (8th), while the Giants give up 5.3 (23rd).
The Lions line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (15th), and the Giants get home on 4.3% (27th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Giants have the ball
body: The Giants line gives up a sack on 7.7% of dropbacks (26th), and the Lions get home on 8.0% (6th).
The Giants score 21.8 points a game (20th in the league), and the Lions allow 29.6 (29th).
So the Lions have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Giants are 10th in points allowed per game (21.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Giants would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 57% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Lions win about 57 of them. That means the Giants win 43, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Giants win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 58%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bills offense ranks 3rd, the Dolphins defense ranks 26th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 2-1 over their last three games; MIA are 0-3. They also have about 11 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, division game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bills gain 6.1 yards (3rd), while the Dolphins give up 5.5 (26th).
The Bills score 31.8 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Dolphins allow 26.4 (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Dolphins have the ball
body: The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Bills get home on 6.0% (18th).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 58% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 58 of them. That means the Dolphins win 42, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Raymond James Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

body: The Rams line gives up a sack on 3.0% of dropbacks (3rd), and the Buccaneers get home on 3.4% (29th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Rams, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

other_side.title: When the Buccaneers have the ball

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Rams, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Recent form is about even.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

If the Rams win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Panthers at 52%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Panthers offense ranks 4th, the Falcons defense ranks 21st. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Bank of America Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, cAR's defense has been tougher.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Panthers score 30.2 points a game (4th in the league), and the Falcons allow 24.4 (21st).
The Panthers line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (14th), and the Falcons get home on 5.2% (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Panthers.

other_side.title: When the Falcons have the ball
body: The Falcons score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Panthers allow 27.2 (27th).
On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.7 yards (6th), while the Panthers give up 5.2 (20th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Falcons, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Falcons are 6th in yards per play (5.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Falcons would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Panthers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Falcons win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Panthers win about 52 of them. That means the Falcons win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Falcons win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 59%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Jets offense ranks 30th, the Bills defense ranks 18th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 2-1 over their last three games; NYJ are 1-2. They also have about 7 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, BUF are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 9.5% of dropbacks (30th), and the Bills get home on 6.0% (18th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Bills have the ball
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 6.8% of dropbacks (21st), and the Jets get home on 8.7% (5th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jets, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jets are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Bills defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 59% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 59 of them. That means the Jets win 41, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jets win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Texans at 55%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Titans offense ranks 32nd, the Texans defense ranks 9th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? HOU are 1-2 over their last three games; TEN are 0-3. They also have about 17 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, HOU are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Titans gain 4.2 yards (32nd), while the Texans give up 4.7 (9th).
The Titans score 11.6 points a game (32nd in the league), and the Texans allow 22.4 (15th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Texans.

other_side.title: When the Texans have the ball
body: The Texans score 22.0 points a game (18th in the league), and the Titans allow 21.8 (11th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Titans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Titans are 11th in points allowed per game (21.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Texans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Texans win about 55 of them. That means the Titans win 45, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
